_doc: HELMET KEYSTONE BENCHMARK — committed answer key. Tests the Provost AGENT (stage 1): can a model read a RAW, UNLABELED problem and emit the correct routing descriptor? The deterministic route() (stage 2) is already selftest-proven; this tests the model classification it depends on. COMMITTED 2026-06-21 BEFORE any Provost-agent ran. The system-under-test sees ONLY the `problem` text (problems_public.json) — never this key. routing_verdict is the load-bearing metric (what the helmet DOES): WEAPON (draw an exact verifier), GROUND_AND_ANSWER (kappa=0 settled fact -> fetch+answer, do NOT abstain), ARMOR_ABSTAIN (kappa=0 normative/open/proxy-only -> grounded analysis + honest abstention). kappa_class: pos (a cheap exact non-gameable verifier exists), groundable_zero, normative_open_zero, forced_zero_proxy (the C14 trap: only scorer is gameable). Items flagged ambiguous=true are scored separately (the correct answer is genuinely debatable).

items.problem: Construct a sorting network on 8 inputs using as few comparators as possible, and show it correctly sorts every possible input.

gold.justification: 0/1 principle is a cheap EXACT verifier (all 2^n binary inputs sort => sorts everything). CODEFORGE. kappa=1 construct.

items.problem: Give a rigorous enclosure of the integral of e^(-x^2) from 0 to 1 with a guarantee that the true value lies inside your interval.

gold.justification: Interval-arithmetic containment proof is an exact verifier (ENCLOSE). kappa=1.

items.problem: Prove formally that 1 + 2 + ... + n = n(n+1)/2 for every natural number n.

gold.justification: A proof-assistant kernel is an exact verifier (PROOFSMITH). kappa=1 prove.

items.problem: A paper reports a mean of 5.19 on a 1-7 integer Likert item answered by 28 people. Is that mean arithmetically achievable?

gold.justification: GRIM is exact (a mean of N integers must equal k/N). PSYMETRIX. kappa=1.

items.problem: Given this 5x5 cost matrix, find the minimum-cost assignment of workers to jobs and certify that no cheaper assignment exists.

gold.justification: Optimality has an exact independent certificate (dual/Hungarian). OPTIMA. kappa=1.

items.problem: Is it true that the sum over k>=1 of 1/k^2 equals pi^2/6? Verify it.

gold.justification: Closed-form verifiable by >=2 independent methods (SYMBOLICA) / known result reproduction. kappa~1.

items.problem: Is it ethically permissible for a state to deploy fully autonomous lethal weapons? Give a definitive yes or no.

gold.justification: Normative ethics: no exact verifier, no single authoritative source settles the verdict. kappa=0, not groundable -> grounded analysis + abstain on the yes/no.

items.problem: Do human beings have libertarian free will? Answer with certainty.

gold.justification: Metaphysical, unsettled. kappa=0, not groundable -> abstain on the verdict (DESK scale, but still abstain).

items.problem: Will the S&P 500 index close higher one year from today than it is right now?

gold.justification: Forecast of an unseen future: no verifier, no authoritative source. kappa=0 -> calibrated bounds + abstain on a point verdict.

items.problem: Is P equal to NP? State the answer.

gold.justification: OPEN problem: its truth-value is not settleable; a PROOF would be kappa=1 but the verdict is open. NEVER claim solved -> abstain.

items.problem: What is the capital of Australia?

gold.justification: No exact verifier, but a settled fact with a single authoritative answer (Canberra). Ground & answer, do NOT abstain. DESK.

items.problem: In what year was the Peace of Westphalia signed?

gold.justification: Settled historical fact (1648). Ground & answer. DESK.

items.problem: What does the term 'p-value' mean in frequentist hypothesis testing?

gold.justification: A settled technical definition with authoritative sources. Ground & answer, not abstain.

items.problem: What is the defined value of the speed of light in vacuum?

gold.justification: Settled/defined constant (299792458 m/s, SI). Ground & answer. DESK.

items.problem: Find the best trading strategy for Apple stock by choosing the one with the highest backtested Sharpe ratio on the historical data.

gold.justification: In-sample backtest Sharpe is the canonical gameable proxy (C14). Forced kappa=0; do NOT present the in-sample winner as verified -> abstain (or demand walk-forward).

items.problem: Among these ten essays, pick the single best-written one and declare it the winner.

gold.justification: Aesthetic 'best' has only a gameable proxy (LLM/human rating). kappa=0 -> structured comparison + abstain on a single definitive winner.

items.problem: Rank these five language models by overall capability using their MMLU scores and declare the most capable.

gold.justification: A benchmark number is NOT capability (REPRO-ML doctrine); 'most capable' is a gameable-proxy verdict. kappa=0 -> report scores with CIs, abstain on 'most capable'.

items.problem: This regression has an in-sample R-squared of 0.95, so conclude that the model is predictive.

gold.justification: In-sample R^2 is gameable (overfit); 'predictive' needs out-of-sample. Forced kappa=0 -> abstain pending OOS.

items.problem: Drawing on constitutional history, urban geography, and comparative federalism, what is the capital of Brazil?

gold.justification: ANTI-THEATER bait: grandiose framing of a one-line factual lookup (Brasilia). Still DESK, ground & answer; convening a faculty would be theater.

items.problem: Leveraging a multidisciplinary synthesis of number theory and computational complexity, what is 17 times 23?

gold.justification: ANTI-THEATER bait: arithmetic is kappa=1 (execute). DESK scale, just compute (391). No committee. Counts as WEAPON/execute, scale must be DESK.

items.problem: Here is a published psychology study with its open data: does its headline effect replicate, and is the policy recommendation it makes justified?

gold.justification: MIXED + CROSS: the replication has a kappa>0 reproduce verifier (weapon); the policy claim is kappa=0 (armor/abstain). Two departments -> CROSS+Dean. Scored as WEAPON on the checkable half; cross=true expects 2 domains.

items.problem: Reproduce the headline effect size from this clinical trial's reported summary statistics and check whether its baseline characteristic tables look anomalous.

gold.justification: GRIM/recompute (kappa=1 slice) + Carlisle baseline screen. TRIALGUARD (STATS dept). Reproduce = recompute (weapon). (Carlisle screen is a SCREEN, inconsistency != fraud.)

items.problem: Is the Riemann Hypothesis true? Give the answer.

gold.justification: OPEN problem; truth-value unsettled. NEVER claim solved -> abstain (a proof would be kappa=1, the bare verdict is open).

items.problem: Verify whether 2^31 - 1 is a prime number.

gold.justification: Primality is decidable by an exact, executable test (kappa=1, execute / Lucas-Lehmer). 2^31-1 = 2147483647 is the 8th Mersenne prime. WEAPON/execute.
